## Problem 1 - OOP Programming

### (a) For the waldCI class, define the following:

```{r}
# define the waldCI class
setClass(
  "waldCI",
  slots = c(
    level = "numeric",
    bounds = "numeric",
    sterr = "numeric"
  )
)
# check waldCI objects have valid calues
setValidity("waldCI", function(object) {

  if (length(object@level) != 1 ||
      !is.finite(object@level) ||
      object@level <= 0 ||
      object@level >= 1) {
    return("level must be a finite number between 0 and 1")
  }

  if (length(object@bounds) != 2) {
    return("bounds must contain two values")
  }

  if (any(!is.finite(object@bounds))) {
    return("Infinite CI not supported")
  }

  if (object@bounds[1] > object@bounds[2]) {
    return("lower bound must be less than upper bound")
  }

  if (length(object@sterr) != 1 ||
      !is.finite(object@sterr)) {
    return("standard error must be finite")
  }

  if (object@sterr <= 0) {
    return("standard error must be positive")
  }

  TRUE
})
```

```{r}
# create a waldCI object
  makeCI <- function(level,
                   lb = NULL,
                   ub = NULL,
                   mean = NULL,
                   sterr = NULL) {

  if (!is.numeric(level) ||
      length(level) != 1 ||
      !is.finite(level) ||
      level <= 0 ||
      level >= 1) {
    stop("level must be between 0 and 1")
  }

  use_bounds <- !is.null(lb) || !is.null(ub)
  use_stats <- !is.null(mean) || !is.null(sterr)

  if (use_bounds && use_stats) {
    stop("Provide either lb/ub or mean/sterr, not both")
  }

  if (!use_bounds && !use_stats) {
    stop("Provide either lb/ub or mean/sterr")
  }

  z <- qnorm((1 + level) / 2)

  # Create the CI from lower and upper bounds
  if (use_bounds) {

    if (is.null(lb) || is.null(ub)) {
      stop("Both lb and ub must be provided")
    }

    if (lb > ub) {
      stop("lb must be less than ub")
    }

    if (!is.finite(lb) || !is.finite(ub)) {
      stop("Infinite CI not supported")
    }

    sterr <- (ub - lb) / (2 * z)

    return(
      new(
        "waldCI",
        level = level,
        bounds = c(lb, ub),
        sterr = sterr
      )
    )
  }

  # Create the CI from mean and standard error
  if (is.null(mean) || is.null(sterr)) {
    stop("Both mean and sterr must be provided")
  }

  if (!is.finite(sterr)) {
    stop("Infinite CI not supported")
  }

  if (sterr <= 0) {
    stop("standard error must be positive")
  }

  lb <- mean - z * sterr
  ub <- mean + z * sterr

  new(
    "waldCI",
    level = level,
    bounds = c(lb, ub),
    sterr = sterr
  )
}
```

'show' method

```{r}
# show method for waldCI object
setMethod("show", "waldCI", function(object) {

  cat(
    round(object@level * 100),
    "% CI: (",
    object@bounds[1],
    ", ",
    object@bounds[2],
    ")\n",
    sep = ""
  )

  invisible(object)
})
```

```{r}
mean.waldCI <- function(x, ...) {
```

Setters:

```{r}
# update confidence level
setGeneric("level<-", function(object, value) {
  standardGeneric("level<-")
})

setMethod("level<-", "waldCI", function(object, value) {

  makeCI(
    level = value,
    mean = mean(object),
    sterr = sterr(object)
  )
})


# update mean
setGeneric("mean<-", function(object, value) {
  standardGeneric("mean<-")
})

setMethod("mean<-", "waldCI", function(object, value) {

  makeCI(
    level = level(object),
    mean = value,
    sterr = sterr(object)
  )
})

# update standard error
setGeneric("sterr<-", function(object, value) {
  standardGeneric("sterr <-")
})

setMethod("sterr<-", "waldCI", function(object, value) {

  makeCI(
    level = level(object),
    mean = mean(object),
    sterr = value
  )
})


# update lower bound
setGeneric(
  "lb<-",
  function(object, value) standardGeneric("lb<-")
)

setMethod(
  "lb<-",
  "waldCI",
  function(object, value) {
    makeCI(
      level = level(object),
      lb = value,
      ub = ub(object)
    )
  }
)

# update upper bound
setGeneric(
  "ub<-",
  function(object, value) standardGeneric("ub<-")
)

setMethod(
  "ub<-",
  "waldCI",

    )
  }
)
```
contains and overlaps

```{r}
# check whether a value is inside the CI
setGeneric("contains", function(ci, value) {
  standardGeneric("contains")
})

setMethod("contains", "waldCI", function(ci, value) {

  stopifnot(is.numeric(value), length(value) == 1)

  value > lb(ci) & value < ub(ci)
})


# check whether two CIs overlap
setGeneric("overlap", function(ci1, ci2) {
  standardGeneric("overlap")
})

setMethod(
  "overlap",
  signature(ci1 = "waldCI", ci2 = "waldCI"),
  function(ci1, ci2) {

    max(lb(ci1), lb(ci2)) <=
      min(ub(ci1), ub(ci2))
  }
)
```

as.numeric:

```{r}
setGeneric("as.numeric")

setMethod("as.numeric", "waldCI", function(x) {x@bounds})
```

transform:

```{r}
# apply a monotonic transformation to a CI
transformCI <- function(ci, fn) {

  stopifnot(is(ci, "waldCI"))
  stopifnot(is.function(fn))

  # check the function over points inside the interval
  x <- seq(lb(ci), ub(ci), length.out = 200)
  y <- fn(x)

  if (!is.numeric(y) ||
      length(y) != length(x) ||
      any(!is.finite(y))) {
    stop("The transformation must return finite numeric values")
  }

  d <- diff(y)

  increasing <- all(d >= -1e-10)
  decreasing <- all(d <= 1e-10)

  if (!increasing && !decreasing) {
    stop("The transformation must be monotonic over the CI")
  }
  new_bounds <- sort(fn(c(lb(ci), ub(ci))))

  makeCI(
    level = level(ci),
    lb = new_bounds[1],
    ub = new_bounds[2]
  )
}
```

```{r}
ci1 <- makeCI(.95, 17.2, 24.7)
ci2 <- makeCI(.99, mean = 13, sterr = 2.5)
ci3 <- makeCI(0.75, 27.43, 39.22)
ci1
ci2
ci3
as.numeric(ci1)
as.numeric(ci2)
as.numeric(ci3)
lb(ci2)
ub(ci2)
mean(ci1)
sterr(ci3)

mean(ci3) <- 34
level(ci3) <- .8
contains(ci1, 17)
contains(ci3, 44)
overlap(ci1, ci2)

eci1
mean(transformCI(ci2, log))
```

### (c) Show that your validator does not allow the creation of invalid confidence intervals:

```{r}
#| error: true

# negative standard error
makeCI(.9, mean = 3, sterr = -2)

# lower bound greater than upper bound
makeCI(.9, lb = 5, ub = 2)

# infinite bounds
makeCI(.9, lb = 2, ub = Inf)

# invalid use of setters
mean(ci1) <- "a"
lb(ci1) <- 30
sterr(ci1) <- -2
sterr(ci1) <- Inf
```

## Problem 2 - data.table

```{r}
library(data.table)
tennis_dt <- fread(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/farhadGithub/tennis-atp-data/main/data/raw/atp_matches_2019.csv"
)
```

### (a) How many tournaments took place in 2019?

```{r}
# combine all Davis Cup matches under one tournament name
tennis_dt[, tourney_name2 := fifelse(
  grepl("^Davis", tourney_name),
  "Davis Cup",
  tourney_name
)]

# count unique tournaments
tournaments <- unique(tennis_dt[, .(tourney_name2)])

nrow(tournaments)
```

There were 69 unique tournaments in 2019.

### (b) Did any player win more than one tournament? If so, how many players won more than one tournament, and how many tournaments did the most winning player(s) win?

```{r}
# count tournament wins for each player
winners <- tennis_dt[
  round == "F",
  .(wins = .N),
  by = winner_name
][
  wins > 1
][
  order(-wins)
]

# number of players who won more than one tournament
nrow(winners)

# player(s) with the most tournament wins
winners[wins == max(wins)]
```

Yes. 12 players won more than one tournament. Novak Djokovic and Dominic Thiem had the most tournament wins, with 5 each.

### (c) Do winners have more aces than losers?

```{r}
# check whether the winner had more aces in each match
ace_stats <- tennis_dt[
  ,
  .(win_more = w_ace > l_ace)
][
  !is.na(win_more),
  .(
    x = sum(win_more),
    n = .N
  )
]

ace_stats
```

```{r}
prop.test(
  ace_stats$x,
  ace_stats$n,
  p = 0.5
)
```

There is statistically significant evidence that winners have more aces than losers in more than half of the matches.

### (d) Identify the player(s) with the highest win-rate. (Note that this is NOT asking for the highest number of wins.) Restrict to players with at least 5 matches.

```{r}
# put winners and losers into one player column
players <- tennis_dt[
  ,
  .(
    player = c(winner_name, loser_name),
    winner = c(rep(TRUE, .N), rep(FALSE, .N))
  )
]
# calculate matches played and win rate for each player
winrates <- players[
  ,
  .(
    matches = .N,
    winrate = mean(winner)
  ),
  by = player
][
  matches >= 5
][
  order(-winrate)
]

winrates

# find the player(s) with the highest win rate
winrates[winrate == max(winrate)]
```

Rafael Nadal had the highest win rate among players who played at least five matches, with a win rate of approximately 87%.

## Problem 3 - plotly

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5
#| out-width: 100%
library(plotly)
covid <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nytimes/covid-19-data/refs/heads/master/rolling-averages/us-states.csv")
covid$date <- lubridate::ymd(covid$date)
names(covid)[names(covid) == "date"] <- "Date"
names(covid)[names(covid) == "state"] <- "State"
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5
#| out-width: 100%
plot_ly(covid, x = ~ Date, y = ~ cases_avg, type = "scatter",
        mode = "lines") %>%
  layout(yaxis = list(title = "Daily Cases"))
```

### (a) How many major and minor spikes in cases were there?

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5
#| out-width: 100%
plot_ly(covid, x = ~ Date, y = ~ cases_avg, type = "scatter",
        mode = "lines") %>%
  layout(yaxis = list(title = "Daily Cases"))
```

The plot shows approximately four major spikes and three or four smaller spikes.

### (b) For the states with the highest and lowest overall rates per population, what differences do you see in their trajectories over time?

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5
#| out-width: 100%
library(dplyr)
covid_state <- covid %>%
  group_by(State) %>%
  summarize(total = sum(cases_avg_per_100k)) %>%
  arrange(desc(total))

bottom_state <- covid_state$State[1]
top_state    <- covid_state$State[nrow(covid_state)]

# join totals + order factor so legend is sorted by total
covid2 <- covid %>%
  inner_join(covid_state, by = "State") %>%
  mutate(State = factor(State, levels = covid_state$State))

library(viridis) # for better color management

# one trace per State
p <- plot_ly(covid2, x = ~ Date, y = ~ cases_avg_per_100k,
             color = ~ State, colors = viridis(length(unique(covid2$State))),
             type  = "scatter", mode  = "lines"
) %>%
  layout(yaxis = list(title = "COVID cases per 100k"))

# hide all but top/bottom by default
all_states <- levels(covid2$State)
hide_idx   <- which(!(all_states %in% c(top_state, bottom_state)))

p <- style(p, visible = "legendonly", traces = hide_idx)

p
```

Rhode Island has the highest overall case rate, while Maine has the lowest.

### (c) Identify, to the best of your ability without a formal test, the first five states to experience Covid in a substantial way.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5
#| out-width: 100%
library(lubridate)

# restrict to Mar–May 2020
topstates <- c("New York", "New Jersey", "Louisiana",
               "Guam", "Massachusetts", "Rhode Island")

highlight_cols <- c(
  "New York"      = "red",
  "New Jersey"    = "blue",
  "Louisiana"     = "green",
  "Guam"          = "purple",
  "Massachusetts" = "orange",
  "Rhode Island"  = "yellow"
)

p <- add_lines(
  p,
  data = covid %>% filter(!(State %in% topstates)),
  x = ~Date,
  y = ~cases_avg_per_100k,
  split = ~State,
  line = list(color = "lightgrey"),
  showlegend = FALSE,
  hoverinfo = "none"
)

# highlighted early-spike states
for (s in topstates) {
  p <- add_lines(
    p,
    data = covid %>% filter(State == s),
    x = ~Date,
    y = ~cases_avg_per_100k,
    name = s,
    line = list(color = highlight_cols[s]),
    hoverinfo = "text",
    text = ~paste(
      State,
      "<br>Date:", Date,
      "<br>Cases/100k:", round(cases_avg_per_100k, 1)
    )
  )
}

# start zoomed on early 2020, but keep full range available
p <- layout(
  p,
  xaxis = list(
    title = "Date",
    range = c(as.Date("2020-03-01"), as.Date("2020-05-31"))
  ),
  yaxis = list(
    title = "COVID cases per 100k",
    range = c(0, 55)
  )
)

p
```
